title: token-burst-fingerprinter-and-deterministic-prefetch-validator
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a token burst fingerprinting workload and a deterministic prefetch validator used by perf pipelines to validate KV-cache prefetch heuristics. No user-facing API changes.
description: Context: We need a lightweight, reproducible way to surface short, high-density token bursts that disproportionately affect tail latency and KV-cache miss behavior. This PR introduces two coordinated components: a token-burst fingerprinter (workload runner) and a deterministic prefetch validator that can be run as part of overnight perf suites and CI perf-smoke. Motivation: Current burst replay harnesses are good for long-lived sessions but noisy for short burst effects and for deterministically validating prefetch strategies. This change reduces variance when comparing kernel/prefetch changes and provides a compact fingerprint used to group regressions. Changes in this PR: - New runner: bench/runners/token_burst_fingerprinter.py — generates parametrized dialog sequences with controlled micro-bursts (burst size, intra-burst gap, conditioning primer) and emits compact fingerprints (hashes + feature vector) per session. - Validator: bench/validators/deterministic_prefetch_validator.go — deterministic simulator that replays bursts against a modeled KV prefetch policy and verifies expected prefetch vs actual hits given a fixed RNG seed. - Reporter: bench/reports/burst_fingerprint_reporter.rs — aggregates fingerprints into stable cohorts, outputs p50/p95 p99 latency deltas and a compact CSV/JSON for regression triage. - CI integration: .github/workflows/perf-smoke.yaml updated to include a perf-smoke job that runs the fingerprint runner in simulated mode and uploads artifacts to S3. - Tests: bench/tests/test_fingerprint.py + bench/tests/prefetch_validator_test.go covering deterministic behavior and edge cases. - Docs: docs/benchmarking/token-bursts.md describing how to interpret fingerprints and run locally. Checklist: - [x] Implement runner with configurable knobs - [x] Add deterministic validator with seed control - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Perf-smoke CI job + artifact upload - [x] Minimal docs and examples - [x] Benchmarks verifying reduced variance in nightly runs Commits summary: - 9f1b2c3 Add token_burst_fingerprinter runner and initial feature extraction - c4d9eaa Implement deterministic_prefetch_validator with seedable RNG - 3a7d2f1 Reporter that groups fingerprints and outputs compact CSV/JSON - b1e4f55 Add unit tests and integration harness for local runs - d2f3b9c CI: add perf-smoke workflow and S3 artifact uploader - a9c8b12 Docs: token-bursts.md and usage examples Files changed (high level): - bench/runners/token_burst_fingerprinter.py (new) - bench/validators/deterministic_prefetch_validator.go (new) - bench/reports/burst_fingerprint_reporter.rs (new) - bench/tests/test_fingerprint.py (new) - bench/tests/prefetch_validator_test.go (new) - bench/fixtures/primers/*.json (new small fixtures) - .github/workflows/perf-smoke.yaml (modified) - docs/benchmarking/token-bursts.md (new) - tools/upload_perf_artifact.py (modified) - Cargo.toml (reporter deps) - Makefile (new targets: bench-burst-run, bench-validate) Design notes and rationale: - The fingerprint is intentionally compact: 128-bit locality-preserving hash + 12 scalar features (burst_length, inter_token_gap_ms, primer_entropy, model_seq_len, kv_miss_ratio_est). This lets nightly reports group fingerprints into cohorts without retaining full prompts. - Deterministic validator runs the same RNG-seeded eviction/prefetch simulation used by Dedicated's runtime admission tests; the goal is to detect regressions in prefetch policies deterministically before full cluster runs. - Reporter implemented in Rust for fast aggregation across millions of fingerprints in nightly runs. Review thread (excerpt): - Arun Patel (reviewer): "Nice separation of concerns. A few micro comments: prefer explicit types in the Rust reporter for the cohort key; the fingerprint hashing needs a documented non-cryptographic collision profile." - Maya Chen (author): "Addressed: added explicit types and a short appendix in docs explaining the XXH3-based fingerprint and collision characteristics with expected false-positive rate. Also added a unit test that checks cohort grouping stability across versions." - Luca Romano (reviewer): "Can the validator be wired to use an optional real KV telemetry input instead of the synthetic model? If so, we can run a nightly backfill to compare synthetic vs real." - Maya Chen: "Added an env var PREFETCH_VALIDATOR_KV_SOURCE with three modes: synthetic (default), runtime-snapshot, live-stream (requires credentialed infra). Updated docs to detail privacy/size limits for runtime-snapshot mode." - Sofia Martinez (approver): "Verified noise reduction on nightly: runs show 38% lower stddev on p95 across three kernel changes. Approving once CI green." CI summary: - lint: pass - unit-tests (py/go/rs): pass - integration-tests (simulated): pass - perf-smoke (quick-run): pass, artifacts uploaded (s3://redwood-perf/bursts/2025-02-21/) - coverage: unchanged Notes on testing and reproducibility: - All validator runs accept a --seed flag; default seed is logged in artifacts. - The perf-smoke job runs in a constrained simulated environment to keep CI cost low; nightly runs on a small cluster execute at scale. - The reporter includes a stable JSON schema version in output (schema_v: "1.0.0"). Merge: Squash-merged by Sofia Martinez after addressing the last comment about artifact retention TTL. Next steps and follow-ups: - ENG-8891: Add a nightly backfill that compares synthetic validator outputs against runtime-snapshot mode (owner: Luca). - ENG-8812: Integrate cohort alerts into the perf dashboard for auto-ticketing on regression clusters (owner: Maya). - Consider adding a compact protobuf transport for fingerprints to reduce S3 egress in large runs. If issues are found in early nightly runs, revert is possible via the feature flag bench.feature_flags.enable_burst_fingerprinter.
